name: Psychology (MA)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
• Completion of 45 units of graduate-level Psychology courses

• A maximum of 18 units may be from lab courses, independent study, outside units, and practica (e.g., 222, 258, 269, 281, 297, 282, 290)

• Successful completion of the First Year Project (FYP) or equivalent master’s thesis
Of the 45 units of Psychology courses, master’s students must complete 4 Core Courses and 2 Statistical Methods Courses as outlined below. These are the same Core Course and Quantitative Methods Course requirements the department sets for PhD students.

rules.name: Core Courses Requirement
rules.desc:
Students must take 5 core courses, each from a different area of the Psychology department: Affective Science, Cognitive Science, Developmental Psychology, Neuroscience, and Social Psychology, as listed below. All core courses must be taken for a letter grade for three units and passed with a B- or better grade.
Consistent with the program’s goal of fostering breadth and engagement across all areas of the department, students are encouraged to take all 5 core courses spanning the five areas of the department. If a student takes 5 core courses, the units and grade of the fifth course are counted toward the student’s advanced units.
rules.notes: Students may be required by their advisors to take up to two additional graduate courses in their area of specialization. The additional courses are counted toward the advanced unit requirement described below in these cases. Students should consult with their advisor about any additional requirements in their area of specialization.

rules.name: Quantitative Methods Course Requirement
rules.notes: Quantitative methods courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a B- or better grade.

rules.name: First Year Project or master's thesis

grading:
All core and stats courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a grade of B- or better.
For advanced units, courses taken for a letter grade must receive a B- or better to count toward the requirement.
reviewNotes: You take four of the five core courses and PSYCH 251 and 252, letter graded with a B- or better (core courses for at least 3 units), toward 45 units, at least 27 of them in graduate Psychology courses other than labs, independent study and practica. Any course taken for a letter grade needs a B- or better to count. The First Year Project or master's thesis is checked by hand.

totals.label: 27 units of Psychology courses other than labs, independent study and practica
